extracted.intended_audience: Researchers/authors reporting observational epidemiologic studies (cohort, case-control, cross-sectional)
extracted.subtask_description: Checklist for preparing reports of observational studies (cohort, case-control, cross-sectional), specifying items that should be included in Title/Abstract, Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, and Other information. Intended to improve transparency and completeness of reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title and abstract — study design term
rubrics_metrics.description: (a) Indicate the study’s design with a commonly used term in the title or the abstract
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make the design explicit (e.g., 'cohort study', 'case-control study', 'cross-sectional study') so readers can immediately identify the study type.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title and abstract — informative balanced summary
rubrics_metrics.description: (b) Provide in the abstract an informative and balanced summary of what was done and what was found
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Abstract should concisely state objectives, key methods (including design/population), principal results with measures of precision, and principal conclusions without overstating findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Introduction — background and rationale
rubrics_metrics.description: Explain the scientific background and rationale for the investigation being reported
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe the context and why the study was done, outlining gaps in knowledge or public health importance motivating the work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Introduction — objectives and hypotheses
rubrics_metrics.description: State specific objectives, including any prespecified hypotheses
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly state primary and secondary objectives and any hypotheses specified before data analysis to distinguish exploratory from confirmatory analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methods — study design
rubrics_metrics.description: Present key elements of study design early in the paper
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clearly state whether the study is prospective/retrospective, and the overall design (cohort, case-control, cross-sectional) and key design features to orient the reader.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methods — setting
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe the setting, locations, and relevant dates, including periods of recruitment, exposure, follow-up, and data collection
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide enough detail on geography, healthcare settings, enrollment and follow-up timeframes so readers can assess applicability and potential temporal biases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methods — participants (eligibility and selection)
rubrics_metrics.description: (a) Cohort study—Give the eligibility criteria, and the sources and methods of selection of participants. Describe methods of follow-up. Case-control study—Give the eligibility criteria, and the sources and methods of case ascertainment and control selection. Give the rationale for the choice of cases and controls. Cross-sectional study—Give the eligibility criteria, and the sources and methods of selection of participants
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (b) Cohort study—For matched studies, give matching criteria and number of exposed and unexposed. Case-control study—For matched studies, give matching criteria and the number of controls per case. Explicitly report inclusion/exclusion criteria, recruitment strategy, sampling frame, and any matching or selection ratios.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methods — variables (definitions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Clearly define all outcomes, exposures, predictors, potential confounders, and effect modifiers. Give diagnostic criteria, if applicable
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide operational definitions and coding for each variable so others can understand and replicate measurement and analysis decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methods — data sources and measurement
rubrics_metrics.description: For each variable of interest, give sources of data and details of methods of assessment (measurement). Describe comparability of assessment methods if there is more than one group
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State instruments, questionnaires, laboratory methods, timing of measurements, and any validation or calibration details; note differences in measurement between groups and how they were handled.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methods — bias
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe any efforts to address potential sources of bias
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report strategies to prevent or assess selection bias, information bias, confounding, and other systematic errors (e.g., blinding, validation, sensitivity analyses).

rubrics_metrics.name: Methods — study size
rubrics_metrics.description: Explain how the study size was arrived at
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe sample size calculations, rationale for sample size or number of events, and any practical constraints affecting study size.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methods — quantitative variables
rubrics_metrics.description: Explain how quantitative variables were handled in the analyses. If applicable, describe which groupings were chosen and why
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State whether continuous variables were analyzed as continuous or categorized, specify cut-points, and justify choices (e.g., clinical relevance, data-driven decisions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Methods — statistical methods (overall)
rubrics_metrics.description: (a) Describe all statistical methods, including those used to control for confounding
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report modelling approaches, variable selection, adjustment sets, and methods used to account for clustering or complex survey design where relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methods — statistical methods for subgroups and interactions
rubrics_metrics.description: (b) Describe any methods used to examine subgroups and interactions
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify prespecified vs post-hoc subgroup analyses, interaction terms tested, and multiplicity considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methods — missing data
rubrics_metrics.description: (c) Explain how missing data were addressed
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report extent and patterns of missingness and methods used (e.g., complete-case analysis, multiple imputation), with assumptions stated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methods — handling loss to follow-up / matching / sampling
rubrics_metrics.description: (d) Cohort study—If applicable, explain how loss to follow-up was addressed; Case-control study—If applicable, explain how matching of cases and controls was addressed; Cross-sectional study—If applicable, describe analytical methods taking account of sampling strategy
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe censoring rules, weighting for sampling, analytic adjustments for matching, and any method used to mitigate follow-up losses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methods — sensitivity analyses
rubrics_metrics.description: (e) Describe any sensitivity analyses
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify additional analyses performed to test robustness of findings to assumptions, alternative definitions, or analytic choices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Results — participants (numbers at each stage)
rubrics_metrics.description: (a) Report numbers of individuals at each stage of study—eg numbers potentially eligible, examined for eligibility, confirmed eligible, included in the study, completing follow-up, and analysed
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (b) Give reasons for non-participation at each stage. (c) Consider use of a flow diagram. Present clear counts and attrition at every stage so readers can assess selection and attrition bias.

rubrics_metrics.name: Results — descriptive data
rubrics_metrics.description: (a) Give characteristics of study participants (eg demographic, clinical, social) and information on exposures and potential confounders
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (b) Indicate number of participants with missing data for each variable of interest. (c) Cohort study—Summarise follow-up time (eg, average and total amount). Include tables showing distributions and missingness to allow assessment of comparability and confounding potential.

rubrics_metrics.name: Results — outcome data
rubrics_metrics.description: Cohort study—Report numbers of outcome events or summary measures over time; Case-control study—Report numbers in each exposure category, or summary measures of exposure; Cross-sectional study—Report numbers of outcome events or summary measures
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide raw counts and appropriate summary measures (rates, proportions, means) by relevant groups and over time as applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Results — main results (estimates and precision)
rubrics_metrics.description: (a) Give unadjusted estimates and, if applicable, confounder-adjusted estimates and their precision (eg, 95% confidence interval). Make clear which confounders were adjusted for and why they were included
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (b) Report category boundaries when continuous variables were categorized. (c) If relevant, consider translating estimates of relative risk into absolute risk for a meaningful time period. Present both crude and adjusted effect estimates with CIs and clear explanation of adjustment sets and rationale.

rubrics_metrics.name: Results — other analyses (subgroups/interactions/sensitivity)
rubrics_metrics.description: Report other analyses done—eg analyses of subgroups and interactions, and sensitivity analyses
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish prespecified from exploratory analyses and report results transparently, including any multiplicity issues or attenuation of effects in sensitivity checks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discussion — key results
rubrics_metrics.description: Summarise key results with reference to study objectives
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Begin the discussion by restating main findings in relation to prespecified objectives and highlight the most important results succinctly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discussion — limitations (bias and imprecision)
rubrics_metrics.description: Discuss limitations of the study, taking into account sources of potential bias or imprecision. Discuss both direction and magnitude of any potential bias
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe limitations candidly (measurement error, residual confounding, selection bias, power), and indicate likely direction and size of bias where possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discussion — interpretation
rubrics_metrics.description: Give a cautious overall interpretation of results considering objectives, limitations, multiplicity of analyses, results from similar studies, and other relevant evidence
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Place findings in context of prior literature, avoid overstating causal claims when not warranted, and consider alternative explanations and consistency with other evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discussion — generalisability (external validity)
rubrics_metrics.description: Discuss the generalisability (external validity) of the study results
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider population, setting, and temporal aspects that limit or support extrapolation of findings to other populations or contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Other information — funding and funder role
rubrics_metrics.description: Give the source of funding and the role of the funders for the present study and, if applicable, for the original study on which the present article is based
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclose funding sources, conflicts of interest, and any influence of funders on study design, data collection, analysis, interpretation, or reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting — stratified reporting for study types and groups
rubrics_metrics.description: *Give information separately for cases and controls in case-control studies and, if applicable, for exposed and unexposed groups in cohort and cross-sectional studies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where applicable, present tables and results stratified by case/control or exposure groups to allow direct comparison and assessment of group-specific measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommended adjunct — Explanation and Elaboration article
rubrics_metrics.description: Note: An Explanation and Elaboration article discusses each checklist item and gives methodological background and published examples of transparent reporting. The STROBE checklist is best used in conjunction with this article.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult the Elaboration article (available from PLoS Medicine, Annals of Internal Medicine, and Epidemiology websites) for detailed methodological background and published examples illustrating each checklist item.
